It supplies the comparison of the relevant structures, moved burden, simultaneous demand and actual dependencies, together with a selected configuration and its conditions. Use that result directly; a selected proposal still needs its effective relations. C.32.MWA clarifies the structures when needed, while A.15.8.MS supplies particular method-use support. Obtain OCE's contributions when assignments, authority, workload or the organization itself must change. Continue here with the helping operations and recipient-facing explanation that the selected arrangement still needs.

Check simultaneous demand on scarce means. Count shared preparation once when its result serves several recipients; case-specific interpretation and help remain recurring work. Two independent demands cannot each consume the same expert hour. A joint review may instead supply current service and coaching in one contribution: count that shared time once, retain setup, recipient effort and additional instructional work, and qualify the service and learning results separately. A qualified AI or provider can replace a contribution when the receiving conditions permit it, not merely because it is cheaper.

Obtain the real commitments. A client must provide promised access; an employer must allocate the employee's time; a volunteer must agree the contribution; a provider must accept the required response window. Where continuing work competes with change, OCE.11 supplies a bounded coexistence and recovery arrangement. Use it once, including its existing results.

If a required condition remains unavailable, compare a smaller slice, another provider, staggered work, another strategy or a revised promise. Preserve a hard protection or authorization condition as a condition, not a disadvantage that a larger benefit can buy away.

#### IS.3:4.6 - Compare complete alternatives at the decision's scale

Use an adequate C.32.MWA.PP comparison directly. When a support choice remains, use the same current baseline, receiving use and relevant horizon. Include preparation, participant time, provider time, tools, coordination, inquiry, retained support, transition and displaced work where they can change the choice. Separate total effort from the demand on a particular scarce contributor.

First remove alternatives that cannot meet the required result or conditions. Then compare the remaining consequential differences: time to usable result, future dependence, human mastery where promised, error exposure, response delay, effort and adaptability. C.11.CRC supplies finite comparison; C.11 supplies the legitimate choice. Do not add unlike ordinal ratings into an unexplained total.

When results differ, make the trade-off explicit. A temporary expert service can be preferable for immediate continuity while a learning arrangement remains necessary for the promised later independence. Combine them only if the additional work and transition are actually supplied. The combination is not automatically the best of both.

Select further inquiry only when its attainable answer could reverse the strategy or permitted conclusion enough to justify its full burden. A bounded first attempt can be the comparison when its protection, recovery and receiving conditions are available. Retain alternatives with an honest limit when no useful comparison is obtainable.

#### IS.3:4.7 - Provide the bounded start and its return

Explain the selected strategy through the receiving case: what becomes possible, how each contribution helps, who supplies it and what changes the next action. Obtain the effective permissions, inputs and commitments before the work that depends on them begins.

Select the observations that can change the attempt. They might concern actual use, fit, burden, the intended learner's contribution or a failed handover. Each has its own subject. A.3.1.MI keeps introduction work, later work, target adaptation, support adaptation and outside results separate.

Return the explained strategy and provided conditions, or the exact unsupported condition and surviving useful work. A strategy description can be complete while the attempt remains blocked by unavailable access. On an observed failure, return to the affected target, contribution or arrangement rather than repeat the entire strategy by default.

### IS.3:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### IS.3:5.1 - Compare complete first-week alternatives

This constructed extension of Harbor Design uses invented quantities to show the comparison. Six analysts are available. After the local diagnosis, suppose four have adequate current capability for the selected case family and two need a supported attempt with feedback. The intended first-week contribution is eight eligible package checks, with the two additional analysts beginning to acquire the missing comparison operation. In the current continuation, the four capable analysts can provide those eight checks at 0.20 hours each, using 1.6 hours already available for checking. The two analysts' acquisition requires additional work.

All three serious alternatives require the same access repair, taking 1.5 technical hours, and a 0.5-hour managerial contribution that makes the review interval and receiving decision effective. These two hours are counted once in each alternative.

| First-week alternative | Scarce qualified provider time | Other direct time, including ordinary checking | Complete effort for the selected work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full six-person workshop, followed by brief individual follow-up | 2 hours preparation + 2 hours teaching + 6 × 0.25 hours follow-up = 5.5 hours | 6 × 2 hours attendance + 6 × 0.25 hours follow-up participation + 2 common hours + 1.6 hours checking = 17.1 hours | 22.6 hours |
| Targeted workplace rehearsal for the two analysts | 1 hour preparation + 2 × 0.75 hours coached rehearsal = 2.5 hours | 2 × 0.75 hours participation + 2 common hours + 1.6 hours checking = 5.1 hours | 7.6 hours |
| Qualified expert supplies the checking contribution for eight cases | 8 × 0.20 hours = 1.6 hours | 2 common hours; the expert replaces the analysts' checking contribution | 3.6 hours |

These totals include the eight checks and the implementation work in the constructed alternatives. Other unchanged package work remains outside this comparison. Relative to the 1.6-hour checking continuation, the additional effort is 21, 6 and 2 hours respectively. Shared workshop time is counted separately for the instructor and each participant because they are different people occupying that interval; replaced checking work is not counted twice. No effect size or learning success is assumed from the arithmetic.

Suppose only three qualified support hours are available after existing commitments. The workshop is unavailable in that window. Targeted rehearsal fits the time limit; that inequality alone does not prove a workable schedule, but the two agreed 45-minute intervals and the preparation time provide one.

Expert execution supplies the immediate result at lower first-week effort. It does not supply the intended analysts' acquired comparison operation. If the recipient requires only the eight immediate checks, that service can be selected. If developing the two analysts is part of the authorized promise, the service is not an equivalent cheaper answer.

The parties select targeted rehearsal for the bounded acquisition attempt and retain the existing qualified review condition until later performance supports another allocation. The actual rehearsal Method and assessment come from HCD and the subject provider. A.3.1.MI examines what happened; the table itself proves neither learning nor the target Method's effectiveness.

#### IS.3:5.2 - Build the local instruction rather than paste a strategy name

The target requires identifying whether a source revision changes the support for a claim. The initial implementation instruction says:

> Use the new review method before release.

A walkthrough shows that the analyst cannot find the source pair and that the technical lead receives only an unqualified approval flag. The local instruction is changed:

> When a package cites a revised source, open the cited edition and the proposed current edition. Locate the passage supporting the claim. State whether the change affects that support, with the relevant passage. Send an unresolved or changed-support case to the technical lead before release recommendation. If either edition is unavailable, return the missing source instead of marking the claim checked.

The source owner supplies the two-edition route. The technical lead agrees the receiving response and timing. The learning provider uses representative pairs to teach the missing comparison where needed. The instruction is a local explanation of the selected operation, not evidence that anyone has performed it.

Now change the condition: a source is a continuously updated database with no recoverable historical edition. The instruction's input condition fails. The helper returns the record-preservation and claim-support question to the source/subject owner. Inventing a timestamp from memory would not preserve the target operation.

#### IS.3:5.3 - Strong AI changes the obtaining way

Suppose a qualified AI service can perform the source comparison under the actual access and protection conditions, and its current evidence supports the required case family. One alternative lets it supply the comparison while the technical lead retains the receiving decision. Another uses it to prepare contrasts for the analysts' practice.

The first can reduce demand for human comparison work without developing analyst mastery. The second can support learning only if the analysts perform the intended operation and obtain suitable feedback. The strategy choice follows the wanted result; it does not preserve a human coach merely because the earlier arrangement had one.

If the service loses access to a protected source, the alternative becomes unavailable for that case. A general capability claim about the AI does not restore the missing input.

### IS.3:6 - Bias-Annotation

The strategy designer can mistake a familiar delivery format for an operative Method, or count the provider's reduced cost while moving work to recipients. Recover the actual case and all consequential participants' effort.

The arithmetic case favors a small initial slice because that is the stated receiving use. A later promise to qualify all six analysts would require its own complete work, support and evidence. Do not reuse the small-case total for that larger result.

### IS.3:7 - Conformance Checklist

- Each serious alternative explains the contribution and operation that could obtain the receiving result.
- An adequate current strategy can be retained without forced novelty.
- Target changes and changes to its introduction or support are distinguishable.
- Local instructions preserve the decisive operation and its input and receiving conditions.
- Qualified people, tools, access, time and permissions can be supplied together.
- Comparison includes the complete additional work and keeps different promised results visible.
- The selected attempt has an actual bounded start, protected conditions and decision-bearing observations.
- An unavailable subject method or provider remains an explicit gap rather than a named box in a plan.

### IS.3:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Misuse | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Select “training” or “facilitation” as though the name explains the intervention. | Describe the actual operation, expected contribution and conditions. |
| Make a local adaptation by deleting the difficult target step. | Obtain a qualified variant or repair the missing means. |
| Count shared preparation once but omit recurring local support. | Follow each actual receiving use and count its demand. |
| Compare expert execution with learning as equivalent outputs. | Preserve the different result and ask the legitimate recipient to choose. |
| Promise the same scarce hour to incompatible service and coaching demands, or count one joint contribution twice. | Obtain a feasible allocation. Where one joint review serves both uses, count its time once and qualify each result separately; retain the additional preparation, recipient and instructional effort. |
| Use a workflow configuration as proof that the Method is enacted. | Inspect the actual performance and its operative conditions through A.3.1.MI. |

### IS.3:9 - Consequences

The strategy becomes performable and revisable: its intended contribution, local work and actual provision can be examined separately. A smaller targeted arrangement or continuing expert service can displace an unnecessary broad programme.

The construction can expose a subject or organization question that support design cannot answer. Its useful result may therefore be an exact required contribution or a narrowed promise rather than a start.

### IS.3:10 - Architectural Rationale

Implementation support combines interventions with different mechanisms and responsibilities. Describing the constituent operations and their receiving relations prevents a bundle of activities from standing in for a Method.

The same account distinguishes Method choice from provision. A good operation can be unavailable; a well-provided service can perform the wrong operation. Comparing both together explains why neither a strategy list nor a staffing chart is sufficient.

### IS.3:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The implementation-support guide's tailoring contribution motivates choosing the kind and intensity of help from the local need rather than a fixed schedule. This pattern develops that choice through actual operations, whole effort and receiving use.

C.32.MWA.PP supplies the developed comparison of performance and provision configurations, including moved burden and simultaneous demands. A.15.8.MS supplies particular method-use support. OCE.11 supplies coexistence with continuing service. A.3.1.MI:4.5 supplies interpretation of delivery, mechanism, adaptation and context. Their sufficient results are used directly; another round of equivalent design or inquiry adds no implementation benefit.

A ready target-specific strategy is the serious simpler alternative. Retain it when its actual conditions fit. The new construction is warranted when a changed input, provider, workload, target or promised result makes that fit consequentially uncertain. The examples show conditional arithmetic and operations, not an empirical superiority claim.

### IS.3:12 - Relations

IS.1 supplies the undertaking and decision boundaries. IS.2 supplies the difficulty and needed contribution. A.3.1.MI performs and interprets the bounded attempt; IS.5 qualifies continuation or changed provision.

C.32.MWA.PP supplies the selected performance and provision configuration when alternative arrangements matter. A.3.2.DE and A.15.8.MS supply reusable explanations and method-use support. HCD supplies human acquisition and assessment. C.32.MWA connects relevant Method, Work, capability and support structures; OCE supplies actual organizational design or change when required. C.11/CRC govern legitimate choice and complete comparison, while C.11.DUA limits further inquiry to a worthwhile attainable contribution.

### IS.3:End


## IS.5 - Sustain, Transfer, Extend or End Implementation Support

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** Stable
>
> **Primary working result:** Continued practice has a feasible support arrangement, or support ends with its remaining work, consequences and receiving responsibilities settled.

### IS.5:0 - Use This When

Use this pattern when an introduction has produced enough experience to decide what help should remain; when a helper, sponsor, tool or source is changing; when another setting wants to use the approach; or when the supported practice is no longer wanted or sufficiently useful.

Begin with one ordinary use that must remain possible and one actual dependency that may change. Find what currently enables that use, including help that is easy to overlook because an expert quietly supplies it. Then decide whether to retain, reduce, replace, transfer, extend or end that contribution. The useful result can be a continuing purchased service. Independence is not an obligatory maturity stage.

Do not run a sustainability project merely because a bounded attempt has finished. If continuing use and its support are already adequately provided, use that arrangement and its ordinary correction route. If no continued use is promised, settle the attempt's actual remaining obligations and stop.

### IS.5:1 - Problem Frame

Implementation support changes while the target practice continues. Temporary experts leave, licences expire, workloads grow, evidence changes, new recipients arrive and an organization transfers responsibility. A practice that worked under unusual attention may become unavailable under ordinary conditions.

Several different continuations are possible. The recipients may want to acquire a missing operation, continue obtaining it from someone else, retain occasional specialist help, substitute a capable AI service or stop using the practice. A community can transmit it among its participants; independent practitioners can also continue using it without forming a communicating community.

The receiving question is therefore how wanted practice remains obtainable, by whom and under which conditions. It is broader than keeping the original support team occupied, but narrower than determining all future development.

### IS.5:2 - Problem

How can the practitioner change or end implementation support without mistaking a successful supported episode for sustainable ordinary use, while avoiding compulsory independence, indefinite assistance and expansion into settings where the result has not been qualified?

### IS.5:3 - Forces

- **Visible performance and hidden rescue.** A recipient can appear independent while another performer resolves every difficult case, repairs inputs or absorbs delay.
- **Continuity and dependence.** A continuing supplier may be the best obtaining way; reliance becomes a problem when the promised contribution cannot actually be supplied.
- **Economy and capability.** Acquiring a capability can reduce some later dependencies but consumes present learning opportunities, feedback and qualified support.
- **Local success and new settings.** An adequate local result can justify reuse without establishing the same result for another population, workflow or consequence.
- **Ending help and ending practice.** These are different changes with different affected parties and remaining obligations.
- **Cultural continuation and control.** Independent carriers can preserve a practice without a service office; participation does not confer authority over their work.
- **Current provision and further development.** Ordinary delivery must continue when wanted, while worthwhile harder problems may demand new target Methods or capabilities.

### IS.5:4 - Solution

#### IS.5:4.1 - Recover the practice that should remain obtainable

Start from the current undertaking and what actual use has shown. State the continuing result, its recipients, important case families and conditions. Separate three questions:

1. Should the target practice continue for this use?
2. What contribution is needed for it to remain obtainable?
3. Who should perform or provide that contribution?

A decision to keep the practice does not answer who should provide it. A decision to end a grant does not establish that its dependent work can safely stop. Use the already sufficient result of A.3.1.MI, including its non-use and adverse results; do not reopen the entire introduction merely because the decision now concerns continuation.

Follow an ordinary case and one consequential variation. Ask what happens when the usual expert is absent, an input is ambiguous, a source changes or demand overlaps with another obligation. Select variations because they can expose a particular dependency, not to demonstrate every conceivable failure.

Recover actual support from the work: who supplies the difficult judgement, restores access, selects the current method variant, detects an obsolete instruction, answers a late question and authorizes an exception? A support contribution can be distributed among a performer, an AI service, a source maintainer and a manager. There need not be a support office or one person who owns them all.

#### IS.5:4.2 - Choose the continuation that obtains the wanted result

For each dependency that matters to continued use, compare the actual alternatives. Use a sufficient current arrangement directly. Otherwise consider:

| Continuation | What must be obtained | What would make the choice inappropriate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retain the present help | A dependable contribution under ordinary demand and agreed terms. | The provider cannot continue, the contribution no longer matters, or its burden exceeds its benefit. |
| Reduce or make help conditional | Recipients can handle the ordinary cases, recognize the named exception and reach support when it occurs. | Apparent independence still relies on unobserved rescue or exceptions cannot be recognized. |
| Transfer provision | Another provider can obtain the required inputs, perform the contribution and be received by the continuing work. | Only files or a role title have moved. |
| Develop recipient capability | Suitable practice, feedback and evidence of performing the required operation. | Personal acquisition is not wanted, or the needed opportunities and time cannot be supplied. |
| Replace the obtaining way | A different qualified source, tool, service or Method can supply the result. | Its limits or access exclude the actual cases. |
| Extend use to another setting | The target and its support fit that setting, or an appropriate adaptation can be qualified. | Local results are treated as a universal adoption instruction. |
| End support or practice | Remaining work and affected dependencies have a legitimate disposition. | A date or funding decision is being used as evidence that dependent work is complete. |

The table distinguishes choices; it does not prescribe a progression. Continuing specialist provision can remain preferable to local acquisition. A highly capable AI service can replace substantial human help where its actual performance and conditions justify the replacement. Conversely, a service that supplies correct answers can leave the recipients unable to notice when it is outside its qualified use.

Compare alternatives against the actual promise. Do not reject a service because it fails to teach when teaching was never needed. Do not call it equivalent to capability development when the recipients must later act without it. IS.3 supplies the connected strategy construction and full work comparison when the continuation requires a new arrangement.

#### IS.5:4.3 - Make transfer a performed receiving connection

Transfer only the contribution whose provider or conditions must change. Recover what the successor needs to recognize, obtain, do, judge and return. Include important exceptions, unfinished cases and the basis of the current qualification. A folder of materials is useful when it actually supplies those needs; its delivery alone is not a transfer of practice.

Have the proposed successor perform or supply a representative contribution under the intended conditions, using an already adequate demonstration where available. Let the real receiver use that result. For a source-review service, the question is not whether the successor can repeat the old expert's explanation, but whether it can obtain the relevant source, make the required comparison and return an interpretable judgement in time.

Identify any continuing dependence on the old provider. A planned overlap can be appropriate; indefinite hidden rescue cannot count as completed transfer. If the successor needs learning, use HCD for the specific acquisition. If it needs permission, staffing, workload protection or access, obtain those conditions through the responsible organization or provider. Training cannot confer authority or create an absent historical record.

Agree what happens to late questions from earlier work. Keep the previous provider's obligation only where it still exists and can be performed; otherwise obtain an actual successor or a legitimate disposition. OCE.11 supplies coexistence and exit from temporary arrangements when this is part of organizational change. Use its full result rather than reconstructing an informal second transfer process.

#### IS.5:4.4 - Qualify ordinary use and maintain the contributions that can change

Use existing evidence when it answers the continuation question under the intended conditions. Obtain another observation only when it can change a decision: for example, whether the recipient recognizes the escalation condition without prompting, or whether a service meets the actual demand when its introductory subsidy ends.

Observe the result and the support consumed. Repeated correct performance with constant expert repair supports the joint arrangement, not independent recipient capability. A single case under ordinary conditions may expose a missing input without estimating a failure rate. Keep the claim at the strength of the evidence.

Provide a correction route proportionate to the consequential change. The performer should know where to return a missing input, questionable answer or obsolete instruction; the responsible supplier must be able to receive that return. A low-risk personal practice may need only a maintained source and an available specialist. A service whose wrong result can harm others may require stronger monitoring, response and interruption arrangements from its governing professional practice.

Different contributions need different maintenance. A target-specific explanation can become obsolete when the target Method changes. A local access instruction can fail after a software change. A support strategy can become unsuitable when recipient preparation or workload changes. A source of research evidence can change the claim about why the practice works. Return each change to the owner of that contribution instead of treating every problem as a need for another learning event.

Where the organization needs a continuing capability to arrange such help, distinguish that capability from the supported subject capability. Its performers must be able to recognize implementation difficulties, obtain qualified contributions and arrange actual support in later cases. Use HCD when acquisition is wanted. Participation in the present introduction does not by itself establish that broader capability.

#### IS.5:4.5 - Extend through changed conditions, not through a success label

A request to extend use starts with the new receiving work. Recover what is already the same and which differences can change applicability or provision. Differences can concern inputs, case distribution, authority, cost of error, available expertise, language, demand or access. Examine the differences that bear on the target operation or the support contribution; an arbitrary catalogue of site characteristics adds no assurance.

Reuse what remains sufficient. A shared explanation, common expert service or reusable exercise can serve several settings. Preserve a local contribution when it depends on the subject matter, available inputs or receiving judgement. For example, one service can maintain the comparison tool, while each technical practice retains its own criterion for whether a changed source defeats a claim.

A new location does not automatically need a full development programme. An equivalent use with adequate existing support may proceed directly. When a difference breaks a relied-on condition, obtain the needed adaptation or return to target selection. IS.2 and IS.3 supply those contributions; A.3.1.MI supplies a bounded introduction when that uncertainty warrants one.

Cultural continuation can require transmission beyond a service contract. Use C.36 to distinguish the needed carriers and transmission relations. Use C.36.RP when access, acquisition or provision must change to make a shared Method obtainable in the receiving setting. CB.14 supplies a joint repertoire undertaking when such work is wanted; its maintained result can also serve independent users. If a communicating community is itself needed, community practice supplies its relationships and maintenance. Do not invent a community requirement for people who can obtain and use the practice independently.

#### IS.5:4.6 - End the contribution without abandoning dependent work

State exactly what ends: the target use, a temporary support service, a provider's participation, a subsidized arrangement or a particular strategy. Identify actual unfinished work and recipients who relied on the contribution. Obtain their disposition through the relevant authority and professional practice.

For a completed low-risk trial with no continuing promise, this may be a short explanation and closure of its remaining questions. For a continuing service, it may require transfer, a fallback or a staged reduction. For a target practice found unfit, it may require stopping its use and restoring a qualified alternative. The implementation-support practitioner does not infer the safe stopping procedure from the fact that support is ending.

Do not keep collecting reports after they can no longer change a legitimate decision. Preserve materials that a continuing receiver needs; do not retain unnecessary personal information merely to document a past programme. Resolve access and custody under the applicable agreement.

End when the promised contribution and actual remaining obligations are complete, transferred or legitimately withdrawn. The old provider's availability can then stop without being silently assumed by the new arrangement. If a necessary receiver or authority is absent, return that unresolved condition plainly; a closing meeting cannot supply it.

#### IS.5:4.7 - Return the next development question to its proper practice

Continued use can reveal a worthwhile harder problem: the old Method reaches its limit, recipients can now undertake more demanding work, or better ways of developing and supporting practice become possible. State the new desired result and the current limit. Return that question to development, subject practice, research or method engineering as appropriate.

Do not automatically label every next challenge an implementation barrier. If a sufficiently useful target Method is unavailable, the next work is to obtain or develop it. If the wanted future result changes, reopen the opportunity and undertaking. Implementation support can help a resulting candidate enter practice without becoming the whole practice of development.

Likewise, successful use need not create an obligation to keep changing. A stable adequate service can remain ordinary work. The question is whether further development is worthwhile and feasible, not whether the implementation programme needs a new cohort to justify its existence.

### IS.5:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### IS.5:5.1 - Transfer a real contribution while keeping current delivery possible

This case is constructed to demonstrate the operations; it is not a reported organizational outcome.

Harbor Design has introduced source-revision comparison. Four analysts already perform the ordinary comparison adequately; two are still acquiring it. A temporary specialist has been resolving unusual references while the technical lead receives release recommendations. The specialist's contract ends in four weeks.

The first proposal is to close support after a final webinar. Following actual use changes the decision: analysts do not know how to resolve an inaccessible superseded source, and the specialist has answered three such questions privately. The ordinary practice therefore depends on source recovery as well as comparison capability.

The source owner can maintain the access route. A subject specialist is available for unusual source interpretation, but only on named days. The technical lead accepts holding the affected release recommendation until a qualified response arrives; urgent work must use a separately qualified route. The successor is not assigned the previous provider's entire role merely because it is available.

A representative transfer case includes an unavailable edition. The analyst returns the missing input, the source owner supplies the recoverable edition, the subject specialist interprets the consequential ambiguity, and the technical lead uses that result. This demonstrates the receiving connection for that case. It does not establish a failure rate or qualification for all technical subjects.

The two learners continue their qualified practice under HCD. The other four do not attend a redundant general course. The temporary provider transfers two unfinished queries to the agreed successors with their actual receiving uses, then ends its participation. If the source owner had no access to the archive, the transfer would remain incomplete despite the webinar and copied materials.

#### IS.5:5.2 - Retain supply by choice, and distinguish it from learning

An independent translator has established the terminology-qualified review workflow in IS.1:5.2. A specialist supplies the rare subject judgements at its review point. When the project-support engagement ends, the translator checks that this contribution remains affordable, dependable, available before delivery and compatible with confidentiality. If it does, retain ordinary provision without creating another support programme. Continued access, intelligible limits and a response to disputed judgements sustain the practice; becoming that specialist is not part of the promise.

Now suppose the translator begins accepting work under conditions where the service cannot be reached. Personal acquisition or another available supplier becomes relevant. The previous service results may help construct learning cases, but they do not prove that the translator can make the required judgement unaided. HCD supplies acquisition and its evidence; IS.3 compares the feasible obtaining ways.

If a qualified AI service becomes available, the same questions apply to its actual cases, inputs, protection and receiving use. Its availability changes the alternatives; the phrase “AI support” does not decide the continuation.

#### IS.5:5.3 - Continue among independent carriers

Several independent repair practitioners use a published diagnostic method. They have no common employer and do not communicate as a community. The source publisher maintains the explanation and a correction channel; each practitioner supplies its own tools and follows the method's applicability limits.

The support question is whether those contributions continue to make the practice available. A maintained correction, discoverable source and actual local access can be sufficient. If a new equipment family breaks an assumption, the publisher needs a qualified method revision or an explicit limit; a new discussion group would not repair the missing diagnostic operation.

A later proposal for peer learning can be useful if its intended contribution warrants the work. It is an additional obtaining way, not evidence that the earlier independent practice was impossible.

### IS.5:6 - Bias-Annotation

Helpers can prefer continuation because it preserves their role, or prefer a clean exit because it improves programme statistics. Return to wanted practice, actual dependencies and remaining obligations.

Recipients can reasonably prefer dependable provision to mastery of a rare operation. Treating independence as the only successful outcome undervalues that choice. Conversely, do not call a service independent merely because the visible performer is local.

### IS.5:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The continuing result and the support contribution that may change are distinguishable.
- Hidden rescue and important exception handling are considered where they affect continued use.
- Retain, reduce, transfer, develop, replace, extend and end are alternatives rather than mandatory stages.
- The selected continuation can obtain its required contribution under ordinary conditions.
- A transfer includes a usable receiving connection and the disposition of unfinished work.
- Evidence supports the actual claim about joint performance, recipient capability or provider substitution.
- Extension reuses sufficient contributions and reopens conditions whose change matters.
- Ending support does not silently abandon continuing work or dictate an unqualified stopping procedure.
- New development questions return to their proper practice rather than becoming endless implementation work.

### IS.5:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Misuse | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Declare sustainability because supported performance was good. | Identify ordinary provision and observe the dependency that is changing. |
| Require every recipient to become self-sufficient. | Compare wanted capability with dependable external supply. |
| Transfer a folder and assume the role has transferred. | Establish that the successor can perform and the receiver can use the contribution. |
| Scale a successful local strategy unchanged. | Recover the new receiving work and consequential differences. |
| Close on a calendar date while late cases still depend on the old provider. | Transfer, complete or legitimately withdraw the actual obligation. |
| Create a community to fix an unavailable technical operation. | Obtain the missing subject contribution first. |
| Turn the next harder development problem into another adoption campaign. | Return the changed target or missing Method to development and subject practice. |

### IS.5:9 - Consequences

Practice can continue through an arrangement whose real dependencies are understood. Support can become smaller, change provider, remain as a service or end without making independence the universal success criterion.

This Method can also justify stopping an arrangement that had looked successful. That is useful when its ordinary conditions cannot be supplied or the target no longer serves the receiving work. It does not guarantee that another arrangement exists.

### IS.5:10 - Architectural Rationale

The continuing practice, its performer capability, its supporting services and its cultural carriers can change independently. Keeping these objects distinct permits a precise transfer or ending instead of forcing every change through one institution.

Continuing support requires work, inputs and performers. When provision ends, settle the commitments to receivers and any unfinished or planned work separately. Ending must therefore respond to the receiving practice and remaining obligations, rather than follow automatically from a completed implementation plan. New development remains a different question even when the same participants supply both contributions.

### IS.5:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The implementation-support guide treats capability-building and leadership as substantive concerns. This pattern preserves the question of continuing capability while allowing qualified supply and chosen dependence where those better serve the work.

OCE.11 supplies temporary coexistence and exit; HCD.15 supplies reconsideration of human development as work and support change; CB.14 supplies a joint repertoire undertaking whose results can reach independent users; C.36 distinguishes cultural continuation beyond one organization; C.36.RP helps make a needed shared Method obtainable. The simpler alternative is to retain an already adequate ordinary arrangement. Additional continuity construction is useful only when a consequential dependency changes or remains unresolved.

### IS.5:12 - Relations

A.3.1.MI supplies the bounded use result and the claims it can support. IS.1 reopens the undertaking when purpose, authority or promised help changes. IS.2 locates a new difficulty; IS.3 constructs a changed support strategy.

C.39, A.3.1.MV and C.32.MWA.PP supply target-method development, variant qualification and provision comparison. OCE supplies organizational changes and the coexistence of ordinary work with temporary change work. HCD supplies desired human acquisition. CB.14 supplies joint repertoire development, C.36 distinguishes cultural continuation, and C.36.RP helps make a needed shared Method obtainable; development and research practices receive changed aims and unavailable subject knowledge. None is replaced by a sustainability label.

### IS.5:End

## IS.6 - Broker a Practice Change Across Unequal Influence

**Type:** Method pattern
**Status:** Stable

### IS.6:1 - Problem frame

Use this Method when a practice change depends on parties whose knowledge, decisions or resources do not reach each other, and unequal influence can prevent a consequential contribution from changing the practice. A referral service may report success while its intended users cannot complete the referral. Staff may know why an intervention fails but reasonably fear the consequences of reporting it. The first useful result is a changed interaction or a clearly located decision that the responsible party can actually take.

The facilitator needs access to the receiving episode and a legitimate way to involve its parties. An ordinary exchange that already gets the necessary contribution to its user can proceed without a brokerage undertaking. Use [CB.15](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb15---connect-practices-through-a-useful-joint-contribution) for a sufficient joint contribution between practices; enter this Method when that contribution must alter the implementation itself.

### IS.6:2 - Problem

Inviting everyone to a meeting can leave the original distribution of influence intact. Collecting more views can also leave the practice unchanged: nobody connects an account of exclusion to an operation, decision or provision condition that can be altered. The broker must build that receiving connection without claiming to represent a group or decide on its behalf merely because it convened the discussion.

### IS.6:3 - Forces

| Force | Consequence for the construction |
| --- | --- |
| Useful disagreement and unequal exposure | People need a way to make a consequential contribution under an acceptable exposure to risk. |
| Local experience and technical judgement | A recipient can expose a failed use; the warranted technical response still needs the appropriate expertise. |
| Distributed decisions | Agreement in one group cannot change another organization's rules, resources or obligations. |
| Speed and meaningful influence | Another consultation is wasteful when it cannot change an action; skipping the excluded party can preserve the wrong action. |

### IS.6:4 - Solution

#### IS.6:4.1 - Find the broken connection in a real use

Follow one consequential episode from the proposed practice to the result its recipient needs. Locate where an input, interpretation, decision or response fails to arrive. Ask who knows that difference, who can act on it and who bears its consequences. Begin with an observed or explicitly constructed episode rather than a complete stakeholder inventory.

Use [PSDA.12](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psda12---recover-participants-concerns-and-affected-systems-for-a-decision-support-inquiry) when the affected parties, concerns or representation are incomplete. Its result identifies whose contribution is missing and why that changes the inquiry. Use [CB.15](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb15---connect-practices-through-a-useful-joint-contribution) to construct the joint work through which otherwise separate practices can exchange and use a contribution. Bring back the actual receiving operation and permission, not merely the name of a stakeholder or another meeting invitation.

#### IS.6:4.2 - Make influence and exposure actionable

For the identified connection, recover who can approve the change, withhold a needed input, impose a consequence or prevent an account from being heard. Include the facilitator's own employer, sponsor and service obligations where they affect candour. Ask affected parties what would make their contribution unsafe or unusable; do not infer consent from their attendance or claim anonymity when a case is identifiable.

[PSDA.13](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psda13---facilitate-decision-support-inquiry-and-preserve-material-dissent) supplies the appropriate inquiry and protection of material dissent. It can produce separate interviews, a carefully attributed account or another usable mode of discussion. [OCE.10](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce10---choose-a-response-to-participation-or-working-culture-difficulties-in-the-target-organization) is needed where actual sanctions, workload, access or participation conditions must change. Receive the changed condition or preserve the limit. A private interview cannot by itself make retaliation impossible, and an assurance of confidentiality cannot grant permission to disclose personal data.

When collective representation is necessary, [CB.16](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb16---form-and-carry-a-collective-voice-into-a-decision) establishes whom the representative can speak for, about what, and how the represented participants can correct that account. Do not make a willing participant represent every absent beneficiary. A materially missing group remains a limit on what the current result can decide.

#### IS.6:4.3 - Translate the contribution into a changeable practice claim

Work with the speaker and the intended receiver on the same episode. Recover what the account changes: the expected benefit, a necessary action, a condition of access, the permitted target population, a harmful consequence or the explanation of why the practice should work. Ask the speaker whether the receiving paraphrase preserves the consequential difference. Retain disagreement that changes the decision.

For each such difference, construct at least the incumbent continuation and the materially different response. A report that appointments are inaccessible might call for a different referral route, assistance with transport, changed opening hours, another provider or a narrower promise. The response is selected through its actual usefulness and feasibility, not by the broker's preference for participation. IS.3 supplies the comparison of complete helping arrangements; IS.7 develops the coupled intervention-and-context question when needed.

#### IS.6:4.4 - Obtain the decision and the receiving connection

Take the interpretable alternative to the party that can decide or supply it, together with the affected parties' account, remaining disagreement, conditions and likely consequences. State what each participant is agreeing to. Use [OCE.6](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce6---establish-holder-assignments-and-enabling-relations-for-organization-change) when an organizational assignment or enabling relation must become effective. An external partner's promise needs that partner's acceptance; a local sponsor cannot confer it.

Let the parties rehearse or perform the changed connection at the smallest useful scale. The referrer supplies the changed request; the receiver shows how it will be acted on; the service recipient can expose an unusable step. Where such a trial is inappropriate, use already sufficient evidence or return the missing authorization. Brokerage ends in an obtainable response, a supported refusal, or the exact unresolved dependency. Consensus is neither required nor sufficient.

#### IS.6:4.5 - Return consequences to the people and the practice

Check the change at the point that motivated the brokerage. Did the previously lost contribution alter the practice, and did the altered practice become usable for its intended recipient? Use A.3.1.MI for the distinction between delivered change, participant response and outside result. If the contribution was heard but could not change an action, return that constraint plainly; do not report it as inclusion accomplished.

Give affected parties a usable explanation of what was decided, what remains unresolved and how a consequential new episode can reach the responsible party. Maintain the connection only for a continuing need or obligation. If observation contradicts a relied-on claim about the practice, return that claim to its owner; if the recipients need to maintain the connection themselves, use IS.8.

### IS.6:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### IS.6:5.1 - A referral exists but cannot be used

In a constructed community-service example, staff report that 30 referrals were issued. Recipients describe a different result: the only appointment window overlaps with their work and the receiving agency rejects incomplete requests. The service sponsor proposes a reminder campaign. Separate conversations under PSDA.13 show that staff had stopped reporting rejections after being blamed for low completion. Before asking staff to report further cases, the responsible manager uses OCE.10 to stop treating rejection reports as individual performance failures and provide a separate review of contested treatment. Staff decide which details from their accounts may be shared; identifiable cases retain their disclosure limits.

The broker and the two agencies use CB.15 to follow a de-identified referral together. The receiving agency distinguishes a necessary input from information that can be obtained at the first contact. The responsible owners compare a revised request, a later appointment window and the reminder-only incumbent. The latter cannot address either observed failure. One agency accepts a bounded change in its intake; the other supplies the revised request and an escalation contact. Neither agreement authorizes another agency's change.

The first returned result is that the revised requests can be received under the agreed conditions. Subsequent observation can examine whether recipients obtain the intended service. Thirty issued requests remain thirty issued requests; the broker does not transform them into thirty successful outcomes. If the later window cannot be staffed, its unavailable provision returns to IS.3 rather than being hidden by better communication.

#### IS.6:5.2 - A community without managerial authority

Independent professionals want a shared case-review practice. Less established participants will not expose client material to prominent peers. The convenor obtains a protected case format and a trial with consenting participants through CB.15/PSDA.13. It cannot order attendance or declare that a volunteer represents all professionals. If the parties can already exchange useful cases on acceptable terms, that sufficient arrangement ends the brokerage question. Expansion requires its own receiving conditions.

### IS.6:6 - Bias-Annotation

Sponsor visibility can make its account appear complete. Familiar representatives can obscure absent recipients. A facilitator may prefer harmony because disagreement threatens its contract. Test these pressures against the specific contribution lost and the action that would change, rather than treating every difference of influence as the same problem.

### IS.6:7 - Conformance Checklist

- A real or explicit proposed episode identifies the lost contribution, its knower, receiver and consequence.
- Protection and representation are supplied where needed; their actual limits remain visible.
- The recovered account changes an interpretable practice claim or explains why it cannot yet do so.
- The proper owner supplies the decision or a supported stop; the broker does not invent authority.
- Observation returns to the affected people and receiving practice, with activity and outside result distinguished.

### IS.6:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Misuse | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Invite a low-influence group but leave every consequential decision unchanged. | Follow its contribution to the operation or condition it could change; report a blocked connection when none is available. |
| Remove disagreement to obtain a shared statement. | Preserve the disputed premise and its consequence through PSDA.13; decide only what the remaining grounds permit. |
| Promise that a protected channel removes all risk. | Obtain the actual protection, disclose its limits and use a different participation arrangement when needed. |

### IS.6:9 - Consequences

The practice can use knowledge that its original decision arrangement excluded. This can require a changed promise, extra receiving work or an unpopular correction. The Method makes those consequences visible; it does not guarantee agreement, equal power or a particular service outcome.

### IS.6:10 - Architectural Rationale

CB.15 supplies joint work, PSDA.12 and PSDA.13 supply the inquiry and OCE supplies organizational changes. The distinctive receiving construction here converts their results into a changed implementation and returns its consequences. Removing that connection leaves useful consultation without the promised change of practice.

### IS.6:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The [2020 ISP Practice Guide](https://implementation.fpg.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/ISP-Practice-Guide.pdf), in its brokering and power-differential sections, connects otherwise separated participants and gives beneficiary experience a consequential place. This Method adopts that question and develops its receiving connection through the full FPF suppliers above. Its alternative is an adequate direct exchange: that cheaper path remains preferable when influence does not defeat the needed contribution.

[Buchanan, Filiatreau and Moore (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43058-024-00572-1) argue for a community-oriented relation among implementation actors. This is a field-position argument, not an effect estimate for the present Method. The constructed cases do not establish effectiveness. Reopen the construction when the proposed protection or representation excludes a consequential experience, or when practice evidence supports a better way to carry it into change.

### IS.6:12 - Relations

IS.1 supplies the undertaking; IS.2 can locate the gap; IS.3 compares the resulting help; A.3.1.MI interprets the changed practice; IS.5 handles continuation. CB.15, PSDA.12 and PSDA.13, CB.16 and OCE.6/10 supply the specific contributions named in Solution. IS.7 receives a coupled adaptation question; IS.8 receives the need to develop the next broker's performance. These are conditional connections, not a mandatory circuit.

### IS.6:End

## IS.7 - Facilitate a Practice Change with Its Participants and Context

**Type:** Method pattern
**Status:** Stable

### IS.7:1 - Problem frame

Use this Method when a proposed practice cannot become useful through delivery of its instructions alone: what it asks people to do interacts with their professional judgement, the people receiving its effects, local work and conditions outside the team's control. The facilitator helps the parties obtain and adapt a workable combination, retaining the evidence and limits on which each change depends.

The first useful result is an explained, obtainable response to one consequential interaction. A sufficient established implementation recipe can be used directly. If the substantive practice is unavailable or its safety cannot be judged, obtain the target profession's contribution before attempting the dependent change.

### IS.7:2 - Problem

A list of barriers identifies neither the response nor its owner. Training staff cannot supply absent equipment; changing equipment cannot answer a justified objection to the practice; local enthusiasm cannot alter an external funding rule. Conversely, replacing the whole intervention because one contribution was not delivered can discard a useful practice. The facilitator must turn the interaction into an appropriate action and then reconsider it through actual use.

### IS.7:3 - Forces

| Force | Practical consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence and local experience | Each qualifies particular claims; apparent conflict needs interpretation before a practice is changed. |
| Adaptation and retained function | A convenient local form may alter the mechanism or a protection on which the useful result depends. |
| Internal knowledge and independent challenge | A local facilitator knows the work but may share its blind spots or lack room to question it. |
| Immediate delivery and recipient capability | Supplying the result and helping recipients learn to obtain it are different, sometimes compatible undertakings. |
| Local action and external conditions | A useful change may depend on a decision beyond the implementation team. |

### IS.7:4 - Solution

#### IS.7:4.1 - Recover the intended practice through a receiving episode

Start with IS.1's undertaking and a sufficient IS.2 diagnosis when available. Recover the target operation, intended benefit, affected people and an ordinary episode in which the result is needed. Ask the target practitioner to explain the professional basis: what is known, which function the proposed action serves, what can vary and what requires renewed judgement. Ask the recipient to show how the proposed result enters their life or work. An intervention's research label does not settle either account.

Keep three kinds of ground distinguishable. Research can support a claim under studied conditions. Professional experience can reveal a workable operation or a failure that research did not examine. Recipient experience can identify a benefit, burden, exclusion or mismatch that a service indicator missed. Relate each to the exact claim it bears on. Use the target profession and an attainable inquiry when the unresolved difference changes what may be attempted. Do not settle a technical claim by vote or dismiss an experienced harm because it was absent from the study's outcome measure.

#### IS.7:4.2 - Explain the interaction that changes the next action

Follow the episode through the proposed practice, its participants and its setting. Locate the dependence: an action requires a kind of input, judgement, cooperation, protection, permission or provision that is not actually obtainable. Examine local work, the containing organization and external conditions only where their contribution could change the response. A local roster, organizational incentive and external eligibility rule are different conditions with different owners.

Use [FPF C.40.JD](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c40jd---develop-a-way-its-holder-and-its-provision-together) for the complete general construction of changing the way, its holder and its provision together. The facilitation-specific question is how the particular intervention's warranted function, recipient experience and service conditions fit that construction. State the live rival explanations before selecting an adaptation. For example, non-use may reflect an unavailable occasion, a burdensome operation, a justified rejection or a help strategy that failed to deliver its contribution. A.3.1.MI:4.5 supplies the delivery–mechanism–context comparison and the observation needed to distinguish them.

#### IS.7:4.3 - Select what to change and who can change it

Construct a response for the identified dependence. The alternatives can change the target practice, the facilitation, participant preparation, provision or several coupled contributions. Show how each proposed response reaches the intended result. Preserve an already sufficient contribution and use IS.3 for its whole arrangement rather than repeat the comparison.

| Located interaction | Receiving action |
| --- | --- |
| An essential operation is not understood or cannot yet be performed. | Obtain the relevant explanation, demonstration or practice through the target Method and HCD; verify the contribution in the receiving episode. |
| The operation is possible but ordinary work prevents it. | Obtain OCE.9/11's organization-capability or coexistence result, with actual capacity and enabling relations. |
| Participant experience exposes a wrong function, burden or access assumption. | Reopen the target or strategy claim; use IS.6 when unequal influence prevents that account from affecting the change. |
| A local variant changes a relied-on function or condition. | Obtain subject judgement and [FPF A.3.1.MV](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#a31mv---construct-and-maintain-a-method-variant)/[FPF A.3.1.FT](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#a31ft---qualify-method-fit-and-transfer); keep the variant's status and fit limits. |
| A required condition belongs to another organization or external authority. | Take an interpretable request and its receiving consequence to that owner; retain the dependent stop until an adequate result is supplied. |

The table locates a supplier, not a diagnosis from a symptom. A staff objection may correctly expose an unsuitable practice. A shortage may be real or a consequence of the chosen workflow. Trace the episode before treating either as a training need.

#### IS.7:4.4 - Fit the facilitation to the work and the people

Choose the facilitating contribution and its performer together. An internal facilitator can work close to the episode and remain available; an external facilitator can bring unfamiliar expertise or a position from which difficult assumptions can be challenged. A paired arrangement can join those contributions, but requires a usable division of work and time. An internal title does not confer trust or authority, and an external contract does not confer technical competence or independence.

Use [FPF C.32.MWA.PP](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c32mwapp---construct-and-compare-method-performance-and-provision-arrangements) to compare the complete arrangements when those differences matter. Include actual access, credibility for the needed interaction, relevant expertise, discretion to adapt, response time and scarce capacity. [FPF A.15.8.MS](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#a158ms---configure-methodological-support-for-work) supplies explanation, tools and other methodological provision. Match less experienced facilitators with an obtainable experienced contribution for the difficult judgement; name what the less experienced performer may decide and when it must return. This is a work arrangement, not an obligation to create a permanent senior post.

Decide whether the facilitator should perform a contribution, work alongside the people learning to perform it, demonstrate it or observe their attempt and give feedback. Select from the present undertaking, risk and wanted capability. An AI may help compare materials or examine a proposed explanation; actual consent, confidentiality, competence, permissions and affected participants' ability to correct that account remain relevant conditions. The source evidence for human facilitation does not establish autonomous AI facilitation's effectiveness.

#### IS.7:4.5 - Prepare and perform a bounded change

Work through the selected episode with those who must act and those who receive it. Make the new receiving connections obtainable: inputs, instructions, permissions, timing, equipment and responses. [OCE.6](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce6---establish-holder-assignments-and-enabling-relations-for-organization-change) establishes changed organizational relations; [OCE.11](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce11---coordinate-organization-change-work-with-continuing-service) reconciles the attempt with ongoing service. Obtain outside commitments from their actual owners. If a required condition cannot be supplied, compare a smaller legitimate attempt, another arrangement or a stop.

Use A.3.1.MI for introduction and observation. Keep the target baseline and the facilitating contribution distinct enough to interpret the result. Observe what was delivered and how it was used before attributing an outcome. Where target and facilitation must change together, preserve the coupled account rather than pretend to isolate an effect. A larger research conclusion goes to its own inquiry Method.

#### IS.7:4.6 - Adapt the exact contribution and return the next question

Interpret the observations through A.3.1.MI:4.5. A missing facilitator action reopens its provision; a delivered action with an unsuitable response reopens its mechanism or local fit; a consequential recipient account can reopen the target itself. Reuse observations that already answer the choice. Keep an unresolved causal explanation visible when a bounded, well-grounded next action is still possible.

Use IS.5 to retain, transfer, extend or end the arrangement. Use IS.8 when participants are to conduct a subsequent change themselves. If successful use reveals that the next useful result requires a different aim or a not-yet-developed Method, return to [FPF C.40.OD](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c40od---construct-and-continue-open-ended-development), [FPF C.40.NP](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c40np---continue-from-a-result-to-new-attainable-problems) and the relevant profession. The end of one implementation is compatible with continuing inquiry and development.

### IS.7:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### IS.7:5.1 - The handover practice and its unavailable conditions

A constructed service team is introducing a handover practice. The subject specialists have qualified its required information and protection conditions. Initial records show that the agreed conversation often does not occur. A generic barrier checklist suggests motivation training. Following actual episodes shows that the incoming team is assigned elsewhere during the overlap and cannot access one necessary record.

An internal facilitator can arrange a local rehearsal but cannot alter the cross-team schedule. The responsible manager receives an OCE.11 coexistence proposal and the data owner receives the access question. Removing the required comparison would change the target practice, so the facilitator does not quietly delete it. While one authority has not answered, a protected rehearsal with already accessible material can test the explanation; it cannot establish that ordinary service has been changed.

After the enabling conditions are supplied, A.3.1.MI examines whether the conversation actually occurs, whether the needed information is used and what the receiving work shows. If the process now occurs but creates an unexpected burden, that result reopens the target or local arrangement. A subsequent improvement in service does not by itself isolate the facilitator's causal contribution.

#### IS.7:5.2 - Choosing a shared or a local facilitator

In a constructed comparison, two sites each need three hours of local episode work per week. One external specialist is available for four hours in total. Assigning it all six hours is infeasible even if a proposal prices only one contract. Suppose each site's existing local facilitator can perform its three hours with one hour of specialist consultation. The joint arrangement then demands two specialist hours and six local hours, plus any actual shared preparation. It is feasible only if those local performers, permissions and protected hours exist. If one site's decisive judgement remains beyond its local performer, the paired arrangement does not meet the same promise.

### IS.7:6 - Bias-Annotation

A familiar framework can make every difficulty look like one of its dimensions. A successful past intervention can make the target seem immune to revision. An enthusiastic local champion can hide a supply constraint. Keep each proposed response tied to its actual episode, responsible owner and conditions of use.

### IS.7:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The target, its professional basis, recipients and actual receiving episode are interpretable.
- The selected interaction explains why a particular action or outside result is needed.
- Target adaptation, facilitation, preparation and contextual change retain their separate claims and owners.
- The facilitating arrangement supplies the required competence, position, discretion, time and receiving connection.
- Observed delivery and use inform the exact adaptation; larger causal or capability claims retain their own qualification.

### IS.7:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Misuse | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Score every contextual factor but leave the next action unexplained. | Follow the consequential interaction to a response, owner and receiving test. |
| Train staff to compensate for an unavailable permission or resource. | Obtain or change the relevant condition; keep the dependent attempt limited meanwhile. |
| Call all local changes harmless adaptation. | Identify the changed operation and condition, obtain subject/variant judgement, and preserve unresolved qualification. |
| Use facilitation as a synonym for holding meetings. | Specify what the facilitator performs and how that contribution changes the recipient's work. |

### IS.7:9 - Consequences

The arrangement becomes adaptable without making the original intervention or the local context untouchable. It requires professional judgement and cooperation that a facilitation contract cannot manufacture. Some useful results are bounded corrections or stops rather than uptake of the originally proposed practice.

### IS.7:10 - Architectural Rationale

C.40.JD supplies the general joint-development construction; IS.3 and A.3.1.MI supply strategy and introduction. Applying those Methods here requires the practice's professional grounds, recipient experience and service conditions to be considered together: a change in one can invalidate a response that appeared adequate in another. The practitioner uses that dependence to select the interaction to change, fit the facilitation to the work and adapt it through observed consequences.

### IS.7:11 - SoTA-Echoing

[Harvey and Kitson's i-PARIHS (2016)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13012-016-0398-2) relates facilitation to innovation, recipients and local, organizational and outer context. The Method adopts that interaction and develops the action-to-owner return rather than treating its dimensions as a sufficient plan. [Mi-PARIHS (2023)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43058-022-00379-y) addresses the move from assessment to tailored facilitation. Its planning-tool and user-feedback results do not establish that the present composition is effective.

[Ritchie and colleagues (2026)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43058-026-01056-0) make the facilitating arrangement more explicit through dimensions including position, activities, flexibility and resources. Adopt the dimensions that change the actual choice; do not require the worksheet as a second plan for every case. These dimensions support design and reporting; they do not establish the effectiveness of a facilitating arrangement. A sufficient target-specific recipe remains the lower-effort alternative when it covers the real conditions. Reopen when a current treatment supplies a better actionable interaction or observations defeat a relied-on fit or mechanism.

### IS.7:12 - Relations

IS.1–3/5 remain independently usable suppliers of agreement, diagnosis, strategy and continuation; A.3.1.MI supplies introduction and interpretation of later use. IS.6 handles influence that defeats the receiving connection. C.40.JD supplies joint development; C.32.MWA.PP and A.15.8.MS supply arrangement and methodological provision; HCD and OCE retain actual human or organizational change. IS.8 develops the recipients' subsequent facilitation performance.

### IS.7:End

## IS.8 - Develop Recipients' Ability to Facilitate Further Practice Changes

**Type:** Method pattern
**Status:** Stable

### IS.8:1 - Problem frame

Use this Method when people or organizations receiving implementation help are expected to recognize and conduct a subsequent change, rather than only maintain the current practice or obtain another expert's answer. Its working object is their performance of implementation facilitation: recovering a consequential difficulty, involving the relevant parties, selecting and obtaining an appropriate response, using observations and adapting what happens next.

The first useful result is one specified facilitation contribution that the intended holder can perform under the promised conditions. Begin with actual work, not a universal competency course. If continuing specialist provision already meets the wanted result and local acquisition is not wanted, use IS.5 directly.

### IS.8:2 - Problem

A successful jointly delivered change can conceal dependence on the expert who recognized the difficulty, asked the decisive question or obtained the missing authority. Transferring slides or ending a contract does not transfer those operations. Yet attempting to make every recipient master every specialty wastes scarce practice time and can remove useful expert provision.

### IS.8:3 - Forces

| Force | Practical consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Current service and developmental work | A learning attempt needs protection without pretending that protected performance is ordinary provision. |
| Local ownership and specialist contribution | Recipients can own a change while retaining expert work they do not need to learn. |
| Observable performance and self-report | Confidence can guide discussion; the claimed ability needs the intended holder's relevant contribution. |
| Immediate success and next challenge | Repeating an already solved case can hide inability to recognize a different difficulty. |

### IS.8:4 - Solution

#### IS.8:4.1 - Specify the subsequent facilitation work and its holder

Identify who is to do what next: a named person, a team with distributed contributions or an organization that must keep the work obtainable. Select a consequential later episode and the support conditions that should remain. The wanted result may be local recognition and referral, a full facilitation undertaking, or the ability to obtain and combine specialists. These are different promises.

Use [HCD.1](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd1--derive-human-capability-demand-from-representative-later-work) for human capability demand and [HCD.3](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd3--diagnose-whether-a-capability-misconception-or-behaviour-limits-work) when its present limitation is uncertain. Use [OCE.9](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce9---realize-a-bounded-organization-capability-increment) for an organization-capability increment; a set of capable people does not alone establish a continuing organizational result. Recover current capability and reuse it. Retained expert judgement, AI assistance or tools belong in the declared conditions rather than being hidden from the capability claim.

#### IS.8:4.2 - Expose the facilitation decisions within joint work

Choose the operations whose acquisition changes the next result. IS.6 supplies the substantive work of making excluded knowledge affect a practice; IS.7 supplies action on the practice–participants–context interaction. A.3.1.MI supplies interpretation of introduction and later use. A learning arrangement needs an adequate account of the facilitation operations it is to teach and a way to supply their professional prerequisites.

During a suitable joint episode, make the consequential decision inspectable. Ask the experienced performer to explain the observed difference, alternative interpretation, chosen action and stopping condition at the moment the recipient can use them. Then let the recipient take a bounded part: for example, reconstruct the lost referral, identify the owner of an external constraint, propose a protected way to obtain a missing account, or explain why a failed result does not yet warrant changing the target. An observer's comprehension of the explanation is useful preparation, not demonstrated performance of that operation.

#### IS.8:4.3 - Arrange practice, feedback and real receiving conditions

For a person's acquisition, use [HCD.9](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd9---perform-deliberate-practice-with-feedback) for deliberate practice with feedback and the appropriate programme/provider Methods when a programme is actually needed. Make the learning attempt and its receiving-work criteria available to the person giving feedback. Feedback should change a particular operation: an omitted participant, an unexplained adaptation, an infeasible demand or a conclusion that exceeds the observation. Merely telling the learner to become more collaborative does not supply that correction.

Use [OCE.18](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce18---arrange-capability-development-and-receiving-work-in-an-organizational-transition) where an organizational transition must provide protected practice time and real receiving work; use [OCE.11](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce11---coordinate-organization-change-work-with-continuing-service) for coexistence with current service. Agree who supplies fallback or takes over when an attempt exceeds its allowed risk. Keep what the recipient performed distinct from rescue supplied by the mentor. Do not withdraw needed assistance merely to create an examination.

Several people can develop complementary operations. A local practitioner may lead episode inquiry while another obtains authorization and an external specialist qualifies a technical adaptation. Test their actual receiving connections as well as each person's contribution. A coordination title cannot fill a missing operation.

#### IS.8:4.4 - Examine a different case before changing the promise

Use [HCD.12](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd12--test-transfer-to-unfamiliar-work-or-learning-from-a-new-source) when the claim concerns the same person's transfer to unfamiliar work. Choose a difference that can defeat the claimed facilitation: another affected group, a newly external condition, a different target mechanism or a conflict between delivered activity and outcome.
